newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 16.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 16.

text.p: Two Gulf of Mexico ports remained shut because of storms in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.

Crude ports Pajaritos remained closed for a fifth consecutive day after storms first shut the port on Saturday afternoon. Dos Bocas crude port reopened at 0800 local/1300 GMT as winds and wave heights relaxed, a port official said.
A port official told Reuters the nation's third largest port will not open later in the day, and that weather conditions will be reviewed early Thursday to decide if the port will be opened.
Winds at Pajaritos were reported between 40 and 50 km per hour, with waves up to 10 feet high. At least 16 petroleum tankers were reported waiting to sail or load from the terminal.

Ciudad del Carmen was also reported closed with winds up to 35 km per hour, but operations at nearby crude port Cayo Arcas did not stop. The crude port reopened early Monday after shutting over the weekend.

Frontera, Nautla, Veracruz, Alvarado, Campeche and Dos Bocas were reported closed to smaller fishing and tourism ships. Smaller vessels were also warned against sailing along the Gulf of Mexico because of winds and wave heights.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Winds mild at maximum 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour), with some clouds and rains over coasts of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan.

Possible rains and strong winds at about 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles) in northern gulf region, with waves four to seven feet. Lower in gulf winds weaker 10 to 15 knots with waves four to six feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with some rains and winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
